references.text: The expression 'to fill the hand' (מִלְאוּ יֶדְכֶם) is a technical term for priestly consecration, which is also used here concerning Aaron and his sons.
Describes the priestly consecration ritual where one 'fills the hands' of Aaron and his sons.
The consecration ceremony for priests in which the expression 'to fill the hands' is used regarding ordination to the priesthood.
Refers to priestly consecration using the expression about filling the hands.
Phinehas shows similar zeal for the Lord and receives a blessing and an everlasting covenant of priesthood as a reward.
Moses blesses the tribe of Levi and refers to their faithfulness at Massah, noting that they did not recognize father or brother when it came to keeping the Lord's covenant.
Continuation of the blessing over Levi, who received the priestly service because of his faithfulness.
The expression 'to fill the hand' is used regarding appointing someone to the priesthood.
Micah 'filled the hand' of a Levite to make him a priest, using the same expression for priestly consecration.
Jeroboam ordained priests ('filled the hands') from anyone, not just Levites.
Jesus teaches that loyalty to him must come before love for family, resembling the principle where the Levites put the Lord above family ties.
Jesus says that a disciple must put him above father, mother, son, and brother in order to follow him.
Both verses deal with the necessity of sanctification (consecration) to meet God's presence or receive his blessing, respectively before and after a major breach.
